sections.name: Why Spicy Food Burns
lines: Spicy food isn't actually hot. It's tricking your nerves.
Chillies contain a chemical called capsaicin.
It switches on the same sensors in your mouth that detect real heat.
So your brain thinks your mouth is on fire. You sweat, your face goes red, and your nose runs.
Water barely helps. Capsaicin is oily, so water just spreads it around.
Milk works better. A protein in it, called casein, grabs the capsaicin and washes it away.
And birds can't feel capsaicin at all. So they eat chillies, and spread the seeds.
